recipes.name: Vinegar all-purpose spray
ing: 10 drops lemon or lavender essential oil (optional)
steps: Pour into a 16 oz spray bottle.
Cap and shake gently.
recipes.uses: Countertops (not stone), sinks, faucets, tile, fridge interiors, trash cans.
recipes.storage: Up to 3 months at room temperature.
recipes.safety: Not for stone, waxed wood or cast iron. Never add bleach or hydrogen peroxide to this bottle.

recipes.name: Castile soap all-purpose spray
ing: 10 drops tea tree or lemon essential oil (optional)
steps: Add the water to a spray bottle first, then the soap (this limits foam), then the oil.
Swirl to mix; don't shake hard.
recipes.uses: Everyday wipe-down of counters, stovetops, sealed wood, baseboards and toys (rinse toys after).
recipes.storage: 1 month. Throw it out if it smells sour or turns cloudy.
recipes.safety: Never mix with vinegar: the acid splits the soap into a greasy film.

recipes.name: Citrus peel vinegar concentrate
ing: Peels of 4 to 6 oranges or lemons
About 3 cups white vinegar, to cover
steps: Pack the peels into the jar and cover them fully with vinegar.
Lid it and keep it somewhere dark for 2 weeks, shaking every few days.
Strain.
To use, dilute 1 part concentrate with 1 part water in a spray bottle.
recipes.uses: Same as the vinegar spray, with a citrus scent instead of a vinegar smell. Cuts light kitchen grease.
recipes.storage: Strained concentrate keeps 6 months; diluted spray 3 months.
recipes.safety: Peels must stay under the vinegar or they mold. Not for stone, waxed wood or cast iron.

recipes.name: Granite and stone cleaner
ing: 1/2 tsp dish soap or castile soap
steps: Combine in a spray bottle and swirl gently.
Spray, wipe, then buff dry with a microfiber cloth.
recipes.uses: Sealed granite, quartz, marble, travertine and other stone where acids aren't allowed.
recipes.safety: Flammable: keep away from flames and heat. Never add bleach.

recipes.name: Kitchen degreaser spray
steps: Dissolve the washing soda in the hot water and let it cool.
Add the soap and pour into a spray bottle.
Spray, wait 2 minutes, wipe, then rinse with a damp cloth.
recipes.uses: Stovetops, backsplashes, cabinet fronts near the stove, greasy appliance handles.
recipes.safety: Wear gloves. Not for aluminum or soft painted or waxed wood. Rinse glass stovetops after.

recipes.name: Oven cleaning paste
ing: About 3 tbsp water, for a spreadable paste
A spray bottle of plain white vinegar, for the rinse
steps: Take out the racks. The oven must be cold and off.
Spread the paste over the oven interior, avoiding heating elements.
Leave 12 hours or overnight.
Scrape with a plastic spatula and wipe with a damp cloth.
Mist any white residue with vinegar and wipe again.
recipes.uses: Oven interiors and doors, baked-on casserole dishes.
recipes.safety: Don't use on self-cleaning oven enamel seals.

recipes.name: Range hood filter soak
ing: Boiling water, enough to cover the filter
steps: Put the filter in a sink or tub and pour the boiling water over it.
Stir in the baking soda slowly (it fizzes), then the soap.
Soak 15 minutes, scrub with a soft brush, rinse and dry.
recipes.uses: Stainless steel mesh hood filters, removable stove knobs, drip pans.
recipes.safety: Baking soda can darken aluminum filters; use hot water and dish soap only on aluminum. Pour boiling water carefully.

recipes.name: Heavy-duty bucket degreaser
steps: Dissolve the washing soda in the hot water in a bucket.
Add the soap.
Scrub with a stiff brush, then rinse with clean water.
recipes.uses: Grill grates, garage floors, outdoor furniture, greasy tools, trash bins.
recipes.safety: Gloves and eye protection. Keep runoff out of storm drains where you can.

recipes.name: Sticky residue remover
steps: Mix into a paste.
Rub onto label glue or sticky residue and wait 5 minutes.
Scrub it off, then wash with soapy water.
recipes.uses: Jar labels, price-tag glue, tape residue, sap on tools.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh, or keep in a lidded jar for 1 month.
recipes.safety: Leaves an oily film until washed. Not for unsealed wood or fabric.

recipes.name: Streak-free glass cleaner
steps: Combine in a spray bottle.
Shake before each use (the cornstarch settles).
Wipe with microfiber or newspaper.
recipes.uses: Windows, mirrors, glass shower doors, chrome fixtures.
recipes.safety: Flammable while wet. Not on tinted car windows with film unless the maker allows alcohol.

recipes.name: Soft scrub cream
ing: 5 drops lemon or tea tree essential oil (optional)
steps: Stir into a frosting-like paste.
Apply with a damp sponge, scrub, and rinse well.
recipes.uses: Tubs, sinks, stovetop rings, grout, stained mugs, stainless sinks.
recipes.storage: Lidded jar, 2 weeks. Add a splash of water if it dries.
recipes.safety: Mildly abrasive: spot-test on acrylic and high-gloss surfaces.

recipes.name: Toilet bowl cleaner
steps: Sprinkle the baking soda into the bowl and pour the vinegar over it.
Let it fizz 10 minutes, scrub with a toilet brush, and flush.
For rings, drain the bowl first and scrub with a paste of baking soda and a little vinegar.
recipes.uses: Toilet bowls and hard-water rings.
recipes.storage: Mix in the bowl, never in a closed container.
recipes.safety: Never use with or right after bleach or a store-bought bowl cleaner. Flush twice between products.

recipes.name: Daily shower spray
steps: Combine in a spray bottle.
After each shower, mist the walls and doors. No rinse needed.
recipes.uses: Prevents soap scum and hard-water spots on tile, glass and fixtures.
recipes.safety: Not for natural stone showers; use the granite and stone cleaner there.

recipes.name: Grout and mildew stain spray
ing: 3% hydrogen peroxide, undiluted, with a spray nozzle on its own bottle
For a paste: 1/2 cup baking soda plus enough peroxide to wet it
steps: Spray the mildew stains and wait 10 minutes.
Scrub with an old toothbrush and rinse.
Use the paste on stubborn grout lines.
recipes.uses: Grout, caulk, shower curtains, window tracks.
recipes.storage: Keep peroxide in its original brown bottle with a screw-on spray top. Mix the paste fresh.
recipes.safety: Can lighten colored grout and fabric. Never combine with vinegar or bleach.

recipes.name: Drain freshener
steps: Pour the baking soda down the drain, then the vinegar.
Cover the drain for 15 minutes.
Flush with the hot water.
recipes.uses: Monthly freshening of kitchen and bathroom drains; slow drains from soap buildup.
recipes.safety: Not a clog remover. Never use after a store-bought drain cleaner, which can splash back. Boiling water can soften PVC joints.

recipes.name: Vinegar rust soak
ing: Undiluted white vinegar, enough to cover the item
1 tbsp salt per cup of vinegar (optional, speeds it up)
1 tbsp baking soda in a bowl of water, to neutralize
steps: Submerge rusty tools, bolts or hardware for 12 to 24 hours, checking every few hours.
Scrub with steel wool or a wire brush and rinse.
Dip in the baking soda water, dry completely, and wipe with a light oil.
recipes.uses: Hand tools, nuts and bolts, cast hardware, garden tools.
recipes.safety: Long soaks can pit thin metal and dull chrome. Gloves recommended.

recipes.name: Citric acid rust bath
steps: Dissolve in a plastic bucket.
Submerge the items for 4 to 12 hours.
Scrub, rinse, dry and oil. Re-season cast iron afterward.
recipes.uses: Bigger batches of rusty parts, bike chains, cast iron restoration.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh; it weakens as it works.
recipes.safety: Gloves and eye protection when handling the powder. Never mix with bleach.

recipes.name: Baking soda rust paste
steps: Make a thick paste and spread it on light surface rust.
Wait 1 hour.
Scrub with a toothbrush or a ball of foil, rinse and dry.
recipes.uses: Light rust on knives, sink rings, chrome, and painted metal where acid would harm the paint.
recipes.safety: Gentle and safe for most finishes after a spot test.

recipes.name: Lemon and salt rust-stain remover
steps: Sprinkle the salt on the stain and squeeze the lemon over it.
Rub it in and wait 1 to 2 hours (in the sun for white fabric).
Rinse, then launder.
recipes.uses: Rust stains on white cotton and linen, porcelain sinks, tub drips.
recipes.safety: Can fade colored fabric, so spot-test. Not for stone. Never pretreat with bleach in the same session.

recipes.name: Kettle and coffee maker descaler
ing: 1 tbsp citric acid powder per 2 cups water (or 1 part white vinegar to 1 part water)
steps: Fill the kettle or reservoir.
Heat it or run a brew cycle, then let it sit 20 minutes.
Empty it, then boil or run 2 cycles of clean water.
recipes.uses: Kettles, coffee makers, showerheads (soak in a bag), faucet aerators, dishwasher monthly.
recipes.safety: Check the appliance manual first; some espresso machines need their own descaler.

recipes.name: Powdered laundry soap
ing: 1 bar (about 4.5 oz) plain castile or laundry bar soap, finely grated
1 cup borax (or a second cup of washing soda for a borax-free version)
steps: Grate the soap with a fine grater or food processor.
Stir all three together in a lidded container.
recipes.uses: 1 tbsp per regular load, 2 tbsp for heavy soil. Low-sudsing, so it works in HE machines. Dissolve it in warm water first for cold washes.
recipes.storage: Airtight, dry container, 6 months or more.
recipes.safety: Label clearly: borax and washing soda are harmful if swallowed. Can fade some dark colors. Not for wool or silk. It's true soap, so in hard water run a vinegar rinse monthly.

recipes.name: Liquid laundry soap
steps: Dissolve the washing soda in 4 cups very hot water in a bucket.
Stir in the rest of the water and the castile soap.
Cool and pour into a gallon jug. It may gel; shake before use.
recipes.uses: 1/2 cup per load in any machine.
recipes.safety: Wear gloves while mixing the hot washing soda water.

recipes.name: Stain pre-treatment
steps: Mix in a small bowl just before use.
Dab onto stains and wait 10 to 30 minutes.
Wash as usual.
recipes.uses: Sweat, food, grass and blood stains on white and colorfast fabric.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh. Pressure can build in a capped bottle.
recipes.safety: Peroxide can lighten dyes, so spot-test. Not for silk or wool.

recipes.name: Vinegar fabric softener rinse
ing: 10 drops lavender essential oil per gallon of vinegar (optional)
steps: Pour into the softener compartment or add during the rinse cycle.
The vinegar smell rinses out.
recipes.uses: Softens fabric, removes soap residue, reduces static, freshens towels.
recipes.storage: Keeps indefinitely in the vinegar jug.
recipes.safety: Never add to a load with bleach. Frequent use can wear rubber seals in some older machines.

recipes.name: Whitening soak
steps: Dissolve in a bucket or the sink.
Soak whites 1 hour to overnight.
Wash as usual.
recipes.uses: Gray socks, dish towels, yellowed pillowcases, baby clothes. A chlorine-free alternative to bleach.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh and never cap it.
recipes.safety: Gloves. Never add chlorine bleach or vinegar to the soak.

recipes.name: Scented wool dryer balls
ing: 2 to 3 drops lavender or eucalyptus essential oil per ball (optional)
steps: Toss the balls into the dryer with each load.
Add oil only when the balls are fully dry, and let it soak in 10 minutes before use.
recipes.uses: Replaces dryer sheets; softens and cuts drying time.
recipes.safety: Use low heat with oiled balls, and never add oil mid-cycle.

recipes.name: Foaming hand soap
ing: 1 tsp jojoba, sweet almond or fractionated coconut oil (optional, for dry skin)
10 drops lavender or orange essential oil (optional)
Distilled water to fill a 10 to 12 oz foaming pump
steps: Add the water first, leaving 2 inches of space.
Add the soap, oil and essential oil, and swirl gently.
Wash hands for at least 20 seconds.
recipes.uses: Kitchen and bathroom sinks. Soap lifts germs off your hands rather than killing them, and that's all it needs to do.
recipes.storage: 2 to 4 weeks. Throw it out if cloudy or off-smelling, and wash the pump between batches.
recipes.safety: Keep essential oils at 1% or less for skin; skip them for babies and sensitive skin.

recipes.name: Liquid dish soap
ing: 1 tbsp washing soda dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water
steps: Dissolve the washing soda in the hot water.
Combine everything in a squeeze bottle and shake gently.
Use 1 to 2 squirts in a basin of hot water.
recipes.uses: Hand dishwashing.
recipes.safety: Hand wash only: never in a dishwasher, where it oversuds. Castile can leave a film in hard water; a vinegar rinse removes it.

recipes.name: Dishwasher detergent powder
steps: Mix in a large bowl, breaking up lumps, and store airtight.
Use 1 tbsp per load in the detergent cup.
Fill the rinse-aid compartment with white vinegar.
recipes.uses: Automatic dishwashers.
recipes.storage: Airtight jar with a silica packet; it clumps in humidity. 3 months.
recipes.safety: Label clearly and keep from children. Hard on hand-painted china and aluminum; wash those by hand.

recipes.name: Bleach disinfecting solution
ing: 5 tbsp (1/3 cup) regular unscented bleach (5 to 9% sodium hypochlorite) per 1 gallon room-temperature water
Or 4 tsp bleach per quart of water
steps: Open a window and put on gloves.
Add the bleach to the water (not water to bleach) in a labeled bucket or bottle.
Clean the surface first, then apply and keep it visibly wet for at least 1 minute.
Wipe or let air dry. Rinse food-contact surfaces with clean water after.
If your bleach bottle has its own directions, follow those instead.
recipes.uses: Hard, non-porous surfaces: sinks, toilets, trash cans, door handles, high chairs.
recipes.storage: Make fresh daily. It weakens after 24 hours.
recipes.safety: Never mix with vinegar, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide or any other cleaner. Don't use splashless or scented bleach. Bleaches fabric and corrodes metal.

recipes.name: Alcohol surface sanitizer
steps: Spray a clean surface so it stays wet at least 30 seconds.
Let it air dry.
recipes.uses: Phones, keyboards, remotes, light switches, faucet handles, stainless steel.
recipes.safety: Flammable: no use near flames or a hot stove. Can damage some screen coatings, lacquer and acrylic. Don't water it down. Never mix with bleach.

recipes.name: Hydrogen peroxide sanitizing spray
ing: 3% hydrogen peroxide, undiluted, with a spray nozzle screwed onto the original brown bottle
steps: Spray a cleaned surface.
Leave it wet 5 to 10 minutes, then wipe.
recipes.uses: Cutting boards, counters, sinks, toothbrush holders, kids' toys (rinse after).
recipes.storage: Opened bottles lose strength in 1 to 6 months. Pour a little into the sink drain: if it no longer fizzes, replace it.
recipes.safety: Can lighten fabric and colored grout. Never in the same bottle as vinegar.

recipes.name: Liquid hand sanitizer (when soap isn't available)
steps: Measure precisely and stir well in a clean bowl.
Pour into a labeled pump bottle. This gives roughly 65 to 70% alcohol; any less won't work.
Rub on hands until dry.
recipes.uses: Hands, only when soap and water aren't available.
recipes.safety: The FDA does not recommend making your own hand sanitizer, and CDC advises 60 to 95% alcohol. Mismeasuring is the main risk, so buy one when you can. Never use methanol. Poisonous if swallowed: keep from children.

recipes.name: Ant trail spray
steps: Spray ant trails, entry points and the ants, then wipe up.
Repeat daily for a week.
recipes.uses: Erases the scent trail ants follow. Pair with the borax ant bait to reach the nest.
recipes.safety: Not for stone. Peppermint oil is harmful to cats; skip it in cat homes.

recipes.name: Borax ant bait
ing: Cotton balls and small lidded containers with holes punched in the lid
steps: Dissolve the sugar and borax in the water.
Soak cotton balls and put them in the small containers.
Set them along ant trails. Ants carry the bait to the colony; expect results in 3 to 7 days.
recipes.uses: Sugar ants in kitchens, bathrooms and along baseboards.
recipes.storage: The liquid keeps 1 month in a labeled jar.
recipes.safety: Borax is toxic if swallowed. Place baits only where children and pets can't reach.

recipes.name: Insecticidal soap for plants
ing: 1 tbsp liquid castile soap (no degreasers or additives)
steps: Mix in a spray bottle.
Spray aphids, mealybugs, whiteflies and spider mites directly, including leaf undersides, in early morning or evening.
Rinse plants with plain water after a few hours. Repeat every 4 to 7 days.
recipes.uses: Houseplants, vegetable gardens, roses.
recipes.safety: Test on a few leaves first; it can burn ferns, succulents and plants in hot sun. Don't spray bees or open blooms.

recipes.name: Fruit fly trap
ing: A jar, plastic wrap and a toothpick
steps: Pour the vinegar into the jar and add the soap (it makes flies sink).
Cover with plastic wrap and poke 5 or 6 small holes.
Replace every 3 to 4 days.
recipes.uses: Fruit flies and fungus gnats near fruit bowls, drains and trash.
recipes.safety: Also remove the source: overripe fruit and damp drains.

recipes.name: Peppermint spider deterrent
steps: Combine in a spray bottle and shake before each use.
Spray window frames, door thresholds, corners and vents weekly.
recipes.uses: Deters spiders and some crawling insects. Evidence is limited: it's a deterrent, not a kill spray.
recipes.safety: Toxic to cats and harmful to dogs if licked or inhaled heavily. Keep away from fish tanks and birds.

recipes.name: Diatomaceous earth insect barrier
ing: A squeeze duster or soft brush
steps: Put on a dust mask.
Puff a thin, barely visible line along baseboards, behind appliances and into cracks.
Leave 3 to 7 days, vacuum, and reapply. It only works while dry.
recipes.uses: Ants, silverfish, roaches, fleas in carpet, crawling garden pests.
recipes.safety: Food-grade only, never pool-grade. The fine dust irritates lungs. Keep it off pets' faces.

recipes.name: Linen and room spray
ing: 1/4 cup vodka or 91% isopropyl alcohol (helps oils mix and dry fast)
20 to 30 drops lavender, eucalyptus or orange essential oil
steps: Combine in a fine-mist spray bottle.
Shake before each use and mist from 12 inches away.
recipes.uses: Sheets, curtains, couches, closets, car interiors.
recipes.safety: Spot-test fabric; oils can stain silk. Flammable while wet. Don't spray near cats, birds or infants.

recipes.name: Carpet and upholstery deodorizer
ing: 10 to 15 drops essential oil, or 2 tbsp dried lavender buds (optional)
steps: Mix in a jar and shake to break up clumps.
Sprinkle over carpet or upholstery and wait 30 minutes to overnight.
Vacuum thoroughly.
recipes.uses: Carpets, rugs, mattresses, pet beds, car seats.
recipes.safety: Keep pets off until vacuumed. Can clog bagless vacuum filters; empty and tap the filter after.

recipes.name: Stovetop simmer pot
steps: Bring to a boil, then simmer on the lowest heat.
Top up the water every 30 minutes.
Refrigerate between uses.
recipes.uses: Whole-home scent that covers cooking and pet odors without sprays.
recipes.storage: Reuse for 2 to 3 days from the fridge.
recipes.safety: Never leave it unattended; a dry pot can scorch or start a fire.

recipes.name: Fridge and shoe deodorizer pouches
ing: A breathable cotton bag, or a coffee filter tied with string
steps: Fill and tie.
Put an unscented pouch or open box in the fridge.
Put scented pouches in shoes, gym bags and closets.
recipes.uses: Fridges, freezers, shoes, hampers, trash can bottoms.
recipes.storage: Replace every 1 to 3 months. Pour the spent baking soda down a drain with the drain freshener.
recipes.safety: No essential oil in fridge pouches; food absorbs it.

recipes.name: Citrus garbage disposal cubes
ing: Peels of 2 lemons or limes, chopped small
1 cup coarse salt or white vinegar
An ice cube tray and water
steps: Pack the peels into the tray.
Top with the vinegar or salt plus water, and freeze.
Drop 2 or 3 cubes into a running disposal with cold water.
recipes.uses: Scrubs and freshens disposal blades and drains.
recipes.safety: Run cold water while grinding. Never reach into the disposal; use tongs.
